call_points.text: India capacity utilisation ~95%; consolidated ~80%; PCR at 95%.
JK Tornel Mexico hit by supply disruptions and IR issues, now resolved; expects better results ahead.
Domestic markets recorded a healthy volume growth of 21% in FY26, led by a robust 42% growth in the OE market.
Raw material prices are expected to rise by 18-20% in Q1FY27 from Q4 due to ongoing West Asia crisis and rupee weakening.
Company has taken a price hike of 4-5% across products in replacement market and 5-7% in export markets, with further hikes underway.
Board approved an aggregate cost of ₹4,980 Cr for further brownfield expansions for PCR and TBR segments in phases until 2029.
Working capital borrowings reduced significantly from ₹2,378 crores to ₹1,808 crores, highlighting efficient working capital management.

penalties.authority: Deputy Commissioner (ST) III, GST, Large Taxpayers Unit, Chennai -35
penalties.details: The Company has received an Order in Form DRC-07 dated 22nd December 2025, issued under Section 73 of the TNGST Act, 2017. The Order confirms the demand towards denial of Input Tax Credit on supplies received from defaulting vendors for the financial year 2021-22, including cases where the vendors either did not file their GSTR-3B returns or filed the returns as “NIL”. The tax demand amounts to Rs. 1.99 lacs, along with interest of Rs. 1.58 lacs and a penalty of Rs. 0.40 lac.
penalties.impact: There is no material impact on financial, operations or other activities of the Company arising out of such Order.

penalties.authority: Deputy Commissioner (ST) III, GST, Large Taxpayers Unit, Chennai -35
penalties.details: The Company has received an Order in Form DRC-07 dated 22nd December 2025, issued under Section 73 of the TNGST Act, 2017. The Order confirms the following demands: (i) disallowance of tax reduced through GST credit notes issued to customers, on account of non-submission of certificates evidencing reversal of input tax credit by the customers; and (ii) levy of interest on tax payable on value increased through debit notes issued pursuant to upward price revisions, calculated from the date of original supply till the date of issuance of such debit notes. The total tax demand amounts to Rs. 18.92 lacs, along with interest of Rs. 16.54 lacs and a penalty of Rs.2.08 lacs.
penalties.impact: There is no material impact on financial, operations or other activities of the Company arising out of such Order.

penalties.authority: Deputy Commissioner (ST) III, GST, Large Taxpayers Unit, Chennai -35
penalties.details: The Company has received an Order in Form DRC-07 dated 24th December 2025, issued under Section 73 of the TNGST Act, 2017. The Order disallows Input Tax Credit on the following grounds: (i) transport services provided to employees; (ii) other alleged ineligible supplies such as air travel, hotel accommodation, etc., provided to Company executives during official visits; and (iii) levy of interest on delayed payment of GST on invoices liable under the Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM). The tax demand amounts to Rs. 33.07 lac, along with interest of Rs. 22.06 lac and a penalty of Rs. 3.45 lac.
penalties.impact: There is no material impact on financial, operations or other activities of the Company arising out of such Order.

penalties.details: The Company has received an Order dated 26th December 2025 pursuant to the GST Audit for FY 2021–22, passed under Sections 73 of the MGST/CGST Act, 2017 read with Section 20 of the IGST Act, 2017. The Order confirms the demand on the following grounds: 1. Excess outward tax liability reported in GSTR-1 as compared to tax paid in GSTR-3B. 2. Non-reversal of Input Tax Credit (ITC) in GSTR-3B as compared to disclosures made in GSTR-9. The tax demand amounts to Rs.14.25 lac, along with interest of Rs. 11.20 lac and a penalty of Rs. 1.42 lac. Appeal will be filed on or before 23.03.2026 to the Joint Commissioner of Commercial Taxes (Appeals) challenging theTax Credit and imposition of Interest and Penalty.
penalties.impact: There is no material impact on financial, operations or other activities of the Company arising out of such Order.

operating_notes.text: FY26 consolidated revenue reached a record ₹16,327 crore with sales volumes growing 21% YoY in India.
Board approved ₹4,980 Cr capex for TBR and PCR tyres capacity expansion of 210 lakh tyres p.a. by FY30.
Installed capacities were fully utilized across segments in FY26 and at India level utilization was above 90%.
Product mix at consolidated level: TBR 56%, PCR 27%, 2/3W 5%, others 12%; 16-inch+ PCR is 35% of PCR volumes.
India capacity utilisation ~95%, consolidated ~80%; TBR and 2/3W near full, PCR 95%.
₹4,980 Cr Chennai PCR/TBR expansion to add ~24% capacity over four years, ~7% next year.

timeline.summary: Shareholders approved Dr. Nand Gopal Khaitan’s appointment as Director and Independent Director for five years from 9th February 2026 via Postal Ballot on 22nd April 2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹4,223.44 Cr, net profit ₹177.96 Cr.
JK Tyre approved a ₹4,980 Cr expansion plan to add 210 lakh tyres p.a. capacity by FY30.
JK Tyre reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹4,233 Cr and PAT of ₹188 Cr, with FY26 full-year revenue at ₹16,384 Cr and PAT at ₹774 Cr.
JK Tyre & Industries Limited’s Kamal Kumar Manik (Company Secretary) shared the audio recording of Q4 FY2025-26 results conference call on 27th May 2026 via the company website.
JK Tyre reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹4,233 Cr and PAT of ₹188 Cr, with FY26 revenue at ₹16,384 Cr and PAT at ₹774 Cr, alongside a ₹4,980 Cr capex approval.
JK Tyre's Q1FY27 call (10 Aug 2026) reported revenue up 2% YoY to ₹3,956 Cr but EBITD to ₹268 Cr as raw material costs rose ~20% QoQ; net debt rose ₹500 Cr to ₹4,945 Cr.
JK Tyre received a ₹94.86 Cr GST demand notice for FY2022-23 on 29 September 2026.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹4,840.73 Cr, net profit ₹65.07 Cr.
On 23 October 2026, JK Tyre's board approved an investment of up to ₹1.05 Cr to incorporate a wholly owned subsidiary, JK GLOBAL TRADING FZ CO., in Dubai, UAE.
